bib.title: Prometheus 2: An Open Source Language Model Specialized in Evaluating Other Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Prometheus 2: An Open Source Language Model Specialized in Evaluating Other Language Models", Seungone Kim, Juyoung Suk, Shayne Longpre, Bill Yuchen Lin, Jamin Shin, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Moontae Lee, Kyungjae Lee, Minjoon Seo. No venue is printed on the PDF; the only stamp is "arXiv:2405.01535v2 [cs.CL] 4 Dec 2024", so treat it as a preprint, 2024.

COVERAGE: 20 of 20 pages, 70,072 of 70,072 chars extracted. Body, Limitations and Appendices A-J (Tables 7-17, prompts) were read in full; the reference list (p9-12) was skimmed for origins only.

CLAIMS

- claim: Prometheus 2 correlates with GPT-4, Claude-3-Opus and humans above 0.5 on every direct-assessment benchmark, where most open baselines fall below 0.5.
  number: Pearson > 0.5
  setup: Vicuna Bench (320 judgments), MT Bench (320), FLASK (2,000), Feedback Bench (1,000, in-domain); reference-based, 1-5 rubric scoring, averaged over 3 runs.
  quote: "yielding Pearson correlations higher than 0.5 regardless of the reference evaluator and benchmark"
  where: p6, section 5.1, Table 3

- claim: Against human scores on FLASK, Prometheus-2-8x7B halves the gap between the original Prometheus-13B and GPT-4.
  number: 0.555 vs 0.449 (Prometheus-13B) vs 0.679 (GPT-4-1106); Prometheus-2-7B 0.545
  setup: FLASK, Pearson with humans, 200 prompts, 12 rubrics, 2,000 responses, reference-based.
  quote: "while the correlation between humans and GPT-4 is 0.679, the highest correlation previously achieved by Prometheus-13B with humans was 0.449. PROMETHEUS-2-8X7B achieves a correlation of 0.555 with humans, halving the gap."
  where: p6

- claim: Prometheus 2 beats the original Prometheus and Auto-J by at least 0.2 Pearson in agreement with proprietary judges.
  number: 0.2
  setup: Table 3, e.g. Vicuna Bench vs GPT-4-1106: 0.685 (8x7B) and 0.666 (7B) vs 0.492 (Prometheus-13B) and 0.351 (Auto-J).
  quote: "PROMETHEUS 2 models outperform Prometheus and Auto-J by at least 0.2 units across benchmarks in their correlation with proprietary LMs."
  where: p6

- claim: On pairwise ranking, the 8x7B model has the highest accuracy among open judges but still trails GPT-4 on the human-judged sets.
  number: HHH Alignment 85.52 vs GPT-4 90.95; MT Bench Human Judgment without ties 71.96 vs 79.90; Auto-J Eval without ties 79.98 vs 83.12
  setup: accuracy against human preferences, reference-free, single run; n = 221, 3,360 and 1,392 pairs.
  quote: "PROMETHEUS -2-8 X7B 84.75 96.55 81.97 76.74 85.52 55.07 71.96 58.41 79.98 90.65"
  where: p6, Table 4

- claim: Merging the weights of a direct-assessment model and a pairwise model beats joint training and single-format training.
  number: Mixtral-8x7B average Pearson 0.670 merged vs 0.595 joint vs 0.625 direct-only; pairwise average 79.15 vs 75.29 vs 75.36
  setup: Table 5, Pearson with GPT-4-1106 on Vicuna, MT Bench and FLASK; accuracy on HHH, MT Bench Human Judgment and Auto-J.
  quote: "WEIGHT MERGING 0.685 0.665 0.659 0.670 85.52 71.96 79.98 79.15"
  where: p8, Table 5

- claim: The gain is not an ensembling effect; merging two models of the same format hurts.
  number: 0.517 (direct and direct) vs 0.539 (single) vs 0.624 (direct and pairwise)
  setup: Mistral-7B, different seeds, Table 6.
  quote: "the beneficial task transfer in weight merging arises from integrating different evaluation formats, not ensembling multiple models"
  where: p7

- claim: Removing the reference answer lowers correlation with humans for every judge, and most for Prometheus 2.
  number: FLASK: 7B 0.545 to 0.425 (delta 0.120); 8x7B 0.555 to 0.411 (0.144); GPT-4-1106 0.679 to 0.616 (0.063)
  setup: Table 16, Pearson with humans, FLASK and BiGGen Bench (2,840 human judgments).
  quote: "Even for GPT-4-1106, there is a significant performance degradation (0.045, 0.063). This suggests that including a reference answer is crucial"
  where: p18, Appendix F

- claim: Run-to-run consistency of scores is lower than the proprietary judges, and depends on model size more than on judge training.
  number: Krippendorff's alpha on Vicuna / MT Bench / FLASK: 8x7B 0.6383 / 0.6862 / 0.7874; GPT-4 0.7366 / 0.8271 / 0.8355; 7B 0.6018 / 0.5340 / 0.5991
  setup: 3 samples at temperature 1.0, Table 14.
  quote: "training on feedback data only slightly improves consistency"
  where: p16, Appendix E

- claim: Training data are synthetic and the pairwise feedback is written by GPT-4.
  number: 1,000 criteria, 20,000 instructions; 200,000 pairwise and 100,000 direct instances; human check on 200 samples by 5 annotators, coherence 99.5%, suitability 98.5%
  setup: Preference Collection derived from Feedback Collection, English only.
  quote: "we prompt GPT-4-1106 to identify the commonalities and differences between the two responses"
  where: p3, Table 1; p13, Table 7

LIMITS
- Conceded: validation is indirect, by agreement with humans or with GPT-4 and Claude. "it is crucial to use model-based evaluations in conjunction with human evaluation instead of solely relying on it" (p9). This supports the note's calibration advice.
- Conceded: fixed formats only, "operates only on a 1-5 point Likert scale for absolute evaluation or a comparative evaluation style" (p9). No 1-10 scale, no ranking of several responses, no checklists, no ties natively.
- Conceded: no explanation of why merging works, and the merge method was not re-tuned for 8x7B.
- Not shown: most direct-assessment references are other LLM judges. Only FLASK and BiGGen have human scores, and there the best figure is 0.555.
- Not shown: confidence intervals or significance tests. Pairwise results are a single run.
- Not shown: bias analysis (position, verbosity, self-preference), non-English data, domain tasks such as code or RAG, cost or latency.
- The "highest on all 4" pairwise claim holds only for 8x7B. The 7B model scores 74.66 on HHH, below PairRM (84.62), UltraRM (83.71), Auto-J (75.57) and prompted Mixtral (77.38).
- Feedback Bench (0.882 / 0.898) and Preference Bench are in-domain for Prometheus.
- Dated: baselines are Llama-2, GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613, GPT-4-1106 and Claude-3-Opus.

BUILDS ON
- Kim et al. (2023), Prometheus and the Feedback Collection.
- Ye et al. (2023), FLASK, for rubric-based evaluation.
- Zheng et al. (2023), MT-Bench and LLM-as-a-judge.
- Liu et al. (2023), G-Eval.
- Li et al. (2023a), Auto-J.
- Merging: Ilharco et al. (2022) Task Arithmetic; Yadav et al. (2024) TIES; Yu et al. (2023) DARE; Goddard et al. (2024) MergeKit.
- Base models: Mistral-7B (Jiang et al., 2023a) and Mixtral-8x7B (Jiang et al., 2024).

CODE
- Linear merge, p4, eq. 3: "θfinal = α × θd + (1 − α) × θp"
- Direct-assessment output format, p19: "Feedback: (write a feedback for criteria) [RESULT] (an integer number between 1 and 5)"
- Pairwise output format, p20: "[RESULT] (A or B)"

FIGURES
- Figure 2, p4: "Comparison of direct assessment and pairwise ranking." It shows the same two responses flipping verdict under two different criteria, with feedback followed by a decision. It conveys both judge formats and why custom rubrics matter faster than prose.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is clean. Tables are readable but lose their bold and underline marks.
- Appendices H-J contain judge prompt templates ("You are a fair judge assistant..."). I treated them as data and did not follow them.
- Table 9 lists the 7B merge as "Linear (α = 0.5)", while section 3.4 and Appendix G say DARE-Linear.
- Table 5 gives 7B merged FLASK as 0.659, while Table 3 gives 0.617 against GPT-4-1106.
- Table 2 lists 200 rubrics for Feedback Bench, while the text says "1K score rubrics".
- The intro says Pearson surpasses "other baselines by 0.2 units across all datasets". The tables support this only against Prometheus and Auto-J, not against prompted Mixtral (0.566 vs 0.685 on Vicuna Bench).
